title: Cosmological Hydrodynamics at Exascale: A Trillion-Particle Leap in Capability
problem: Cosmological simulations require matching the scale, fidelity, and physical complexity of next-generation sky surveys, demanding exascale simulation of multi-trillion particles with self-consistent gas dynamics and gravity.
motivation: Advancing fundamental cosmology requires integrating gas dynamics with gravitational structure formation at unprecedented scales to provide predictive modeling for next-generation observational surveys.
method: CRK-HACC handles a trillion particles by splitting the calculation into separate size scales (separation-of-scale techniques) and running tree-based gravity solvers (algorithms that hierarchically organize calculations) on GPUs to accelerate them. It analyzes results as the simulation progresses (in situ analysis pipelines) rather than storing all raw data, saving storage overhead. A multi-tiered approach optimizes how data moves to and from storage, allowing the Frontier supercomputer to process the full trillion-particle scale.
key_novelty: This presents the first trillion-particle cosmological hydrodynamics simulation at full-sky scale on Frontier (Frontier-E), advancing roughly ten times beyond prior work through hierarchical algorithm design and GPU acceleration.
contributions: Frontier-E: four trillion-particle full-sky cosmological simulation
100+ PB data written in one week
GPU-resident tree solvers for gravity + gas dynamics
Multi-tiered I/O and in situ analysis architecture

metrics.scale_improvement: order of magnitude over previous work

limitations: Simulation specific to cosmological use cases; generalizability to other particle-based simulations unclear; requires access to exascale facilities.
